title: The Moab and Its Siblings: A Kenyan Hiker's Guide to Merrell Hiking Shoes
meta_title: Merrell Hiking Shoes in Kenya: Best Moab for 4 Trail Types
meta_description: Merrell hiking shoes for Kenya: Moab 3, Moab Speed 2 and MQM 3 matched to local trails and rains, plus sizing and thrifted checks in Nairobi.
excerpt: Which Merrell hiking shoes suit Kenyan trails? We compare the Moab 3, Moab 3 Mid, Moab Speed 2 and MQM 3, explain Merrell sizing and show what to check on a thrifted pair in Nairobi.

content:
Five-millimetre lugs, a cushioned heel and a roomy toe box explain why Merrell hiking shoes are so popular on Kenyan day hikes. Near Nairobi, a Moab 3 GORE-TEX or Moab 3 Mid Waterproof is the right pick in the rains, while the vented Moab and the lighter Moab Speed 2 suit the dry, dusty months.

Choosing is harder than it looks, because the Moab family alone has low, mid, vented, waterproof and Gore-Tex versions, and most Merrell hiking shoes reach Kenya as thrifted pairs rather than boxed stock. Below we match each Merrell line to real Kenyan trails and seasons, explain how the shoes fit, and show what to check on a second-hand pair before you pay.

Quick Facts

  • First boot: Merrell's first boot, the Wilderness, appeared in 1981 after Randy Merrell built boots by hand in the United States.
  • Signature model: the Moab, whose name stands for "Mother Of All Boots", now in its third generation (Moab 3).
  • Grip: Moab 3 and MQM 3 models use a Vibram TC5+ rubber outsole with 5 mm lugs.
  • Waterproofing: "GORE-TEX" versions use a Gore-Tex membrane, "Waterproof" versions use Merrell's own membrane, and "Vented" versions have no membrane at all.
  • Weight: a pair of Moab 3 Mid Waterproof boots weighs roughly 990 g, according to REI's listing.
  • Kenyan sweet spot: Ngong Hills, Karura, Ol Donyo Sabuk and Mt Longonot day hikes; pick something stiffer for loaded treks on Mt Kenya.

What Are Merrell Hiking Shoes Known For?

Merrell hiking shoes are known for comfort straight out of the box. Cushioned midsoles, a forgiving fit and soft suede-and-mesh uppers mean most pairs need little breaking in, which is why beginners and weekend walkers like them.

The brand's own history page says Randy Merrell took apart a pair of cowboy boots to learn how they were made, then built his first hiking boots by hand. The Wilderness boot of 1981 is described there as "the one that started it all", and the Moab arrived generations later as a lighter, more casual hiking shoe. Merrell now calls the Moab the world's number one hiking boot; you can read the company's timeline on the official Merrell history page.

Four pieces of technology turn up on most Merrell hiking shoes, and knowing them makes a label much easier to read:

  • Vibram TC5+ outsole: a rubber compound Vibram makes for Merrell, used on the Moab 3, Moab Speed 2 and MQM 3, with lugs about 5 mm deep.
  • Super Rebound Compound and Air Cushion: a shock-absorbing midsole with an air pocket in the heel, found on the Moab 3.
  • FloatPro foam: a lighter, springier midsole used on the Moab Speed 2, paired with a TPU plate for stability.
  • Kinetic Fit ADVANCED footbed: a removable, contoured insole with heel cushioning and medium arch support.

The flip side of all that comfort in Merrell hiking shoes is support. A Moab is softer and more flexible than a stiff leather trekking boot, so it shines on day hikes with a light pack and asks more of your ankles on rough, loaded descents. Keep that trade-off in mind as you read the model notes below.

Which Merrell Hiking Shoes Suit Kenyan Trails?

For most Kenyan hikers, the Moab 3 GORE-TEX (low) or Moab 3 Mid Waterproof is the best all-round Merrell. Choose the Moab Speed 2 for lighter, faster walking and the MQM 3 for rocky ground and scrambling.

Moab 3: the everyday Merrell hiking shoe

Of all Merrell hiking shoes, the low-cut Moab 3 is the one most Nairobi hikers should try first. It keeps the classic Moab shape, with a rubber toe cap, a bellows tongue that stops grit getting in, and a Vibram TC5+ sole that bites well into dry murram and grassy slopes. On the red-soil climb at Ol Donyo Sabuk or the forest paths at Karura, a low shoe like this feels lighter than any boot.

Read the label carefully. A Moab 3 GORE-TEX or Moab 3 Waterproof keeps out puddles and wet grass, while a Moab 3 Vented is all mesh and drains quickly but lets water straight in. In Kenya the vented shoe makes a good second pair for hot, dry walks such as Hell's Gate in January or February.

Moab 3 Mid: when you want ankle cover

The Moab 3 Mid adds an ankle-height collar and a moulded nylon arch shank. REI lists the Mid Waterproof with pig suede leather and mesh, a Merrell waterproof membrane, a Super Rebound Compound midsole, an Air Cushion in the heel and an 11.5 mm heel-to-toe drop. The higher collar helps keep ash out of your socks on the Longonot rim and offers a little more protection on loose stones.

The Mid is still a soft boot, though. It is comfortable on 6-8 hour day hikes, but it will not hold your ankle the way a Lowa Renegade or a Keen Targhee Mid does under a heavy pack. If you are weighing those options, our guide to Keen hiking boots compares a similar roomy fit with a stiffer build.

Moab Speed 2: lighter and quicker

Among Merrell hiking shoes, the Moab Speed 2 sits between a hiking shoe and a trail runner. It uses FloatPro foam, a full-length TPU plate and a Vibram TC5+ outsole, with a mesh and ripstop upper. It feels quick and springy on hard-packed paths such as the Ngong Hills ridge in the dry season. Some wearers find it runs slightly small, so try your usual size and half a size up.

MQM 3: for rock and scrambling

The MQM 3 GTX has a synthetic mesh and TPU upper, a Gore-Tex membrane, a 6 mm drop and 5 mm Vibram TC5+ lugs; one UK retailer lists it at about 640 g. It suits short, rocky climbs where you use your hands, such as the boulders near the top of Oldoinyo Lesatima, and drier crags like Lukenya.

Are Merrell Hiking Shoes Waterproof Enough for the Kenyan Rains?

Merrell hiking shoes labelled GORE-TEX or Waterproof keep water out well on rainy-season day hikes. Vented versions are not waterproof, and no low shoe stops mud pouring in over the collar.

Kenya has two wet seasons: the long rains from roughly March to May and the short rains from roughly October to December. Around Nairobi that means slick black cotton soil on the Ngong Road side, greasy red murram on the Ngong Hills and deep, cold mud in the Aberdares bamboo on hikes such as Elephant Hill. For those months, look for Merrell hiking shoes with a membrane.

GORE-TEX vs Merrell's own waterproof membrane

Both keep rain out while letting some sweat escape. Gore-Tex is the better-known membrane and tends to cost more new. Merrell's own membrane, sold under names such as M Select DRY on older pairs and simply "Waterproof" on the Moab 3, does the same job for day hikes. On a thrifted pair, the condition of the lining matters more than which membrane it has.

When vented Merrell hiking shoes make more sense

From January to February and again from about June to September, many trails near Nairobi are dry and dusty. A vented shoe lets heat out on the long, exposed climbs at Mt Longonot or Hell's Gate, and dries in an hour after a stream crossing. If you hike all year, a waterproof pair plus a vented pair covers almost every condition.

Whatever you wear, add waterproof leg gaiters for deep mud and long wet grass. Gaiters close the gap at the ankle that even the best low-cut Merrell hiking shoes leave open, and our article on boots for Kenyan trails explains when a full boot is the safer choice.

How Do Merrell Hiking Shoes Fit?

Merrell hiking shoes usually fit true to size or slightly roomy, with a generous toe box. Many hikers with broad feet find them comfortable straight away, and the Moab is commonly made in wide fittings too.

REI's listing notes that reviewers find the Moab 3 Mid Waterproof fits slightly large. The Moab Speed 2 is the exception: several sources say it runs a little small and narrow compared with the classic Moab. That is why trying on matters more than the number on the box.

Reading the size label

Thrifted Merrell hiking shoes in Nairobi come from the UK, Europe and the US, so check the label inside the tongue. It usually lists US, UK and EU sizes side by side. A men's US 9 is roughly a UK 8.5 and an EU 43, but always trust the printed label over a conversion chart. Women's Merrell models use a different last, slimmer at the heel; a woman with a broad foot can sometimes wear a men's Moab comfortably.

A simple fit test

  1. Try shoes in the afternoon, when your feet are slightly swollen, wearing the socks you hike in.
  2. Before lacing, push your foot forward: you should fit one finger behind your heel.
  3. Lace up and walk on a slope or stairs. Your toes should not hit the front on the way down.
  4. Check that your heel does not lift more than a few millimetres as you walk.
  5. Stand on tiptoe. The shoe should crease across the ball of the foot, not press into your toes.

Good socks change the fit as much as the shoe does. Our merino wool hiking socks add a little cushioning and keep feet drier on 6-8 hour days, so bring a pair when you try shoes on.

What Should You Check on Second-Hand Merrell Hiking Shoes?

On second-hand Merrell hiking shoes, check the tread depth, the midsole foam, the bond between sole and upper, and the inside lining. A pair that passes all four still has plenty of hiking left in it.

Quality thrifted gear is how many Kenyan hikers afford a big-brand shoe, and a used Moab can be a smart buy. Soft, cushioned shoes do wear differently from stiff leather boots, though, so work through these checks in order:

  1. Tread: new Moab 3 and MQM 3 lugs are about 5 mm deep. If the lugs under the ball of the foot and the heel are worn flat, grip on wet murram will suffer.
  2. Midsole: press your thumb into the side of the midsole. Deep creases or foam that stays squashed mean the cushioning is tired.
  3. Sole bond: bend the shoe and look along the edge where the rubber meets the upper, especially at the toe cap. Small lifts can be glued; wide gaps usually spread.
  4. Lining and membrane: run your hand inside. Holes at the heel or a torn lining often mean a waterproof shoe no longer keeps water out.
  5. Heel counter: squeeze the back of the shoe. It should spring back, not fold flat.
  6. Insole: a flattened footbed is easy and cheap to replace, so do not let it put you off an otherwise sound pair.

Signs of genuine Merrell hiking shoes

Counterfeit outdoor footwear exists everywhere, so it helps to know what genuine Merrell hiking shoes usually look like. Look for a sewn label inside the tongue with sizes and a style number (Merrell style codes typically begin with the letter J), a crisp Merrell logo, neat and even stitching and, on Vibram-soled models, the small yellow Vibram octagon moulded into the outsole. Gore-Tex versions usually carry a Gore-Tex tag or print. None of these checks is proof on its own, and the price of a shoe is no guide either; take your time and compare details.

Pro Tips for Merrell Owners

  • Match the label to the season: GORE-TEX or Waterproof from March to May and October to December, Vented in the dry months.
  • Lace for descents: pull the laces snug over the instep before the steep drop off Longonot's rim so your toes stay off the front.
  • Swap the insole: a fresh footbed brings a tired but sound pair back to life.
  • Break them in gently: wear new shoes on two or three short walks at Karura or Ngong Road Forest before a big day out.
  • Carry a trekking pole: an ultralight foldable trekking pole makes up for the softer support of a low shoe on loose ground.

Can You Use Merrell Hiking Shoes on Mt Kenya or Kilimanjaro?

You can use Merrell hiking shoes on the lower slopes of Mt Kenya and Kilimanjaro, but most hikers are better off in a stiffer, insulated boot for summit night and long, loaded days.

A Moab 3 Mid GORE-TEX handles the forest and moorland sections of routes such as Sirimon or Machame comfortably. The trouble starts higher up. Summit pushes begin around midnight in temperatures below freezing, and the scree on the way up Point Lenana or Kibo punishes soft midsoles and mesh uppers. Many trekkers wear a comfortable Merrell in camp and on easy stages, then switch to a supportive leather boot for the cold, steep days.

If you are building a full kit, our Mt Kenya packing list covers boots, layers and gloves, and the brand round-up of hiking boot brands for Kenya shows which makers build stiffer mountain boots.

How Do You Care for Merrell Hiking Shoes?

Care for Merrell hiking shoes by brushing off mud after every hike, drying them slowly away from direct heat and re-proofing the suede before each rainy season.

Mud left on the suede of Merrell hiking shoes dries hard and pulls moisture out of the leather, and grit wears through mesh. Knock the worst off at the trailhead, then rinse with clean water and a soft brush at home. Take out the insoles and loosen the laces so air can reach the inside.

Dry them in a shaded, airy spot, stuffed with newspaper that you change after a few hours. Never dry shoes beside a jiko, on a hot iron-sheet roof or against a heater: heat can weaken the glue between sole and upper, which is the most common place a soft hiking shoe fails. Before the long rains and the short rains, spray clean, slightly damp shoes with a waterproofing product suited to suede and fabric. Store them dry, out of sealed bags, so mould does not grow in Nairobi's damp months.

When to replace them

Merrell hiking shoes, like most soft hiking shoes, usually wear out at the midsole before the upper. Once the cushioning feels flat, the lugs are smooth or your feet ache after hikes that used to be easy, it is time for a new pair. Thrifted shoes make that replacement far cheaper than buying new each time.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are Merrell shoes good for hiking in Kenya?

Merrell shoes are good for hiking in Kenya, especially on day hikes near Nairobi such as Ngong Hills, Karura, Ol Donyo Sabuk and Mt Longonot. Their Vibram soles grip dry murram and grass well, and the waterproof versions cope with rainy-season puddles. For loaded multi-day treks or Mt Kenya's summit, most hikers prefer a stiffer, warmer boot.

Is the Merrell Moab actually waterproof?

The Merrell Moab is waterproof only in its GORE-TEX and Waterproof versions, which have a membrane inside the shoe. The Moab Vented has no membrane and lets water in, though it dries quickly. Check the tongue label or the side of the shoe for "GTX", "GORE-TEX" or "WP". Water can still enter over the collar in deep mud.

Do Merrell Moabs run big or small?

Merrell Moabs usually run true to size or slightly large, with a roomy toe box that suits wider feet. The Moab Speed 2 tends to run a little smaller and narrower. Try shoes in the afternoon with your hiking socks on, and make sure you can fit one finger behind your heel before lacing up.

What's the difference between the Moab 3 and the Moab Speed 2?

The Moab 3 is a classic, cushioned hiking shoe with a suede-and-mesh upper and an Air Cushion heel. The Moab Speed 2 is lighter, with FloatPro foam, a TPU plate and a mesh upper, so it feels more like a trail runner. Choose the Moab 3 for rough day hikes and the Speed 2 for fast, dry walks.

How long do Merrell hiking shoes last?

Merrell hiking shoes typically last several hundred kilometres of regular hiking, depending on terrain, weight and care. The midsole foam and the sole bond usually wear out before the upper. Cleaning off mud, drying them away from heat and replacing a flattened insole all help a pair last longer on Kenyan trails.

Final Thoughts

Comfort from the first step is the reason to buy Merrell; your season and your feet decide which one. A Moab 3 GORE-TEX or Mid Waterproof suits most rainy-season day hikes around Nairobi, a vented Moab or Speed 2 suits the dry months, and the MQM 3 handles rock.
